questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid quoting a specific salary figure for governance roles?
options: Because figures go stale quickly and vary enormously by market, and this catalog has no reliable way to verify a precise number as current
Because governance roles never pay a competitive salary
Because salary research is not a useful skill for job seekers
Because only executives are allowed to discuss compensation
questions.explain: The lesson deliberately avoids a specific invented or unverifiable number, teaching the research process instead so the learner builds a current, sourced range for their own market.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does pay and title vary unusually widely for data governance roles compared to some other data roles?
options: Titles aren't standardized, regulated industries tend to fund the role more formally, and the role can sit in different departments (IT, data, or compliance)
Because data governance is not considered a real job by any employer
Because governance roles are always the highest-paid data role at every company
Because governance work requires no specialized skill at all
questions.explain: The lesson lists inconsistent titles, industry regulation intensity, and which department the role reports into as concrete reasons governance pay and scope vary more than some other data roles.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend searching under when researching a governance salary range?
options: Several governance-adjacent title variants, such as Data Governance Analyst and Data Steward, not just one title
Only the exact phrase "Data Governance Analyst" and nothing else
Only job titles containing the word "Chief"
Titles from a completely unrelated field, for comparison
questions.explain: Because titles for this work vary across companies, the lesson recommends researching under multiple governance-adjacent title variants to build an accurate range.

questions.q: What is the recommended response if you're pushed to give a number when asked about salary expectations?
options: Answer with your own researched range rather than inventing a single figure on the spot
Refuse to answer under any circumstances
State the highest number you can think of, regardless of research
Always name a number first to show confidence
questions.explain: The lesson applies the same anchoring principle used elsewhere in this catalog: avoid naming a number first, and if pushed, answer with a researched range instead of an invented figure.

questions.q: Besides the base salary number, what does this lesson say to evaluate before accepting or countering an offer?
options: The whole package — signing bonus, bonus target, remote/hybrid flexibility, review timeline, and certification or conference reimbursement
Nothing else matters besides the base number
Only the company's stock price on the day of the offer
Only the length of the commute to the office
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out evaluating the full offer package, including benefits like certification or conference reimbursement, which is directly relevant to the costs covered in the certifications lesson.
